title: Remote update probe exception
description: Investigate whether macOS --check-update can exit non-zero when the configured remote update URL raises a non-404 urllib exception.
hypothesis: The macOS check-update path only handles HTTP 404 and lets network errors or HTTP 5xx/403 propagate; the API wrapper converts the launcher non-zero exit into HTTP 500.
findings: Observed root cause: packaged macOS launcher fails GitHub HTTPS with SSLCertVerificationError, exits non-zero, and API maps that to HTTP 500.
evidence_for: packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:151-161 uses urllib and only handles HTTP 404; packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:189-196 calls it without catch; packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:410-412 exits 0 only after successful check; main.py:1573-1575 maps non-zero launcher exit to 500; direct run of /Applications/Infinite Canvas.app/Contents/MacOS/Infinite Canvas --check-update failed with SSL CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
evidence_against: Default GitHub macos-VERSION, macos-manifest.json, and macos-app-base.zip returned HTTP 200 via curl from the host, so the remote assets exist.

title: Launcher executable unavailable
description: Investigate whether /api/launcher/check-update returns 500 when the backend is launcher-managed but INFINITE_CANVAS_LAUNCHER_EXE is missing or points to a nonexistent file.
hypothesis: The backend route is reachable only in launcher-managed mode, but call_launcher_command returns HTTP 500 if INFINITE_CANVAS_LAUNCHER_EXE is absent or invalid.
findings: This is a possible 500 path, but not the observed local failure because the live response detail was launcher command failed, not launcher executable missing.
evidence_for: main.py:1550-1556 reads INFINITE_CANVAS_LAUNCHER_EXE and raises HTTP 500 with detail launcher executable missing when empty or missing; main.py:1708-1712 delegates check-update to call_launcher_command.
evidence_against: Live curl to http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/launcher/check-update returned detail launcher command failed, proving the executable was found and launched.

title: Mac bundle bootstrap failure
description: Investigate whether macOS check-update can exit non-zero before remote probing when bootstrap manifest or app-base.zip is missing or corrupt.
hypothesis: The macOS launcher resolves runtime context and reads bootstrap manifest without top-level exception handling, so corrupt/missing bootstrap assets can cause a subprocess failure converted to HTTP 500.
findings: This is a possible 500 path, but not the observed local failure because the direct launcher traceback reached the remote HTTPS fetch.
evidence_for: packaging/macos/launcher/runtime_manager.py:32 parses bootstrap manifest without catch; packaging/macos/launcher/runtime_manager.py:159-172 fingerprints and extracts bootstrap/app-base.zip without catch; packaging/macos/launcher/launcher_main.py:189-196 performs runtime resolution before remote fetch.
evidence_against: Direct launcher traceback failed at urllib.request.urlopen after runtime and manifest steps, so bootstrap was not the current failing point.
